must_remember: Gamma rays are high-frequency electromagnetic waves emitted when a daughter nucleus drops from an excited state to a lower energy state.
Gamma emission does not change the atomic number (Z) or mass number (A) of the emitting nucleus.
The energy of an emitted gamma photon corresponds exactly to the difference between two nuclear energy states: $\Delta E = E_i - E_f$.
Gamma rays interact with matter primarily via three mechanisms: Photoelectric effect, Compton scattering, and Pair production.
The intensity of gamma radiation decreases exponentially with absorber thickness according to the Lambert-Beer law: $I = I_0 e^{-\mu x}$.
Internal conversion is a competing process where an excited nucleus transfers its energy directly to an orbital electron instead of emitting a gamma photon.
Metastable states (nuclear isomers) have relatively long half-lives and are denoted by a superscript 'm' (e.g., $^{99m}\text{Tc}$).
Pair production requires a minimum threshold energy of $2m_0 c^2 \approx 1.02\text{ MeV}$ and occurs in the vicinity of a nucleus.

glossary.meaning: High-frequency, high-energy electromagnetic photon emitted by radioactive nuclei.
A parameter characterizing how easily a volume of material can be penetrated by a beam of light or other radiation.
A radioactive decay process where an excited nucleus interacts electrostatically with one of the orbital electrons of the atom, causing the electron to be ejected.
An excited state of an atomic nucleus with a measurable half-life significantly longer than the typical half-life for nuclear excited states.
The inelastic scattering of a high-energy photon by a free or loosely bound charged particle, typically an electron.
The creation of an elementary particle and its antiparticle, usually an electron and a positron, from a neutral boson such as a high-energy photon.
